The supplied results do not show a paper by Boyd. The closest match on “clinical provenance categorization” is a pilot study on sentence-level clinical provenance categorization for multidisciplinary hospital-stay summarization, which fine-tunes Llama-3 models to label provenance across multi-source clinical notes and tests cross-domain transfer from MIMIC-III to NICU summaries [1].

Related papers use “provenance” differently: one addresses evidence-traceable clinical reasoning with temporal knowledge graphs to close a citation “provenance gap” in rare disease AI [2], another studies over-crediting same-trial evidence in medical verification [3], and another measures redundancy in LLM-generated clinical corpora for provenance classification [5]. So the results cover clinical provenance categorization in general, but not a Boyd-specific categorization.
